provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original task, each foreground (8) cell becomes 2 if its mirror partner in the same column across the horizontal midline (row H-1-r) is also 8. Otherwise it becomes 5. Background cells are unchanged. Under the D4 transform, the optional row reversal (index >= 4) keeps a top-bottom mirror as a top-bottom mirror. An odd number of clockwise rotations turns it into a left-right mirror. So the emitted program compares cell (r,c) with (H-1-r,c) when d4%4 is even, and with (r,W-1-c) when it is odd, working directly in visible coordinates. Colour roles are fixed constants: foreground = palette[8], symmetric = palette[2], asymmetric = palette[5]. All other cells, including background palette[0], are copied unchanged. The middle row or column of an odd-sized grid pairs with itself, so its foreground cells become the symmetric colour. This matches the archived solver.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: grids contain only the background and foreground colours, generated at 6x6, though the code handles any rectangular size. I found no fixture contradictions or constructor defects. The constructor compares grid[row][col] == grid[5-row][col] only for nonzero cells, which is the same as the foreground-partner test. Demonstrations are not needed and are ignored. Nothing has been executed or tested.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Each foreground (8) cell becomes 2 if the cell in the same column on the mirrored row (5-r) is also 8, and 5 otherwise. Background stays 0. The emitted solver applies this directly in visible coordinates. When d4%4 is even it compares (r,c) with (H-1-r,c), using g[::-1,:]. When d4%4 is odd it compares (r,c) with (r,W-1-c), using g[:,::-1]. Colours are palette[8]->palette[2] for paired cells and palette[8]->palette[5] for unpaired cells.
evidence: Constructor: `output[row][col] = 2 if grid[row][col] == grid[5 - row][col] else 5`, applied only when grid[row][col] is nonzero. Inputs contain only {0, 8}, so equality with a nonzero cell means the partner is 8. This matches the factory's `paired = is_fg & (mirrored == FG)`.
No hidden latent decides labels. The output is a deterministic function of the visible input, and the random latents are only the 36 cell bits.
Indexing is correct. 5-row equals H-1-r for H=6, and the column index is unchanged. Archived program and factory both use g[::-1,:] in the base orientation.

D4 axis handling: conjugating a horizontal-midline reflection by a D4 element gives a vertical-midline reflection exactly for the axis-swapping elements (rot90, rot270, transpose, anti-transpose). Those are the elements with an odd quarter-turn count, whether or not a flip is composed in. So `horizontal = (k % 2 == 1)` is correct for indices 0-7.
No whole-grid untransform/retransform wrapper is used. The solver only selects a mirror axis and colour constants, which is a legitimate specialization.

Spot-checked the fixtures against the rule. Test (0,5) and (5,5) are both 8, giving 2 ✓. Test (0,3)=8 with (5,3)=0 gives 5 ✓. Test (1,0)=8 with (4,0)=0 gives 5 ✓. Train 4 (1,5) and (4,5) are both 8, giving 2 ✓.
No ties or ambiguities: the outcome is a binary test per cell.
Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants, no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The solver assumes inputs contain only background and foreground. Any other colour would be copied unchanged. The constructor never produces other colours, so this does not matter in-domain.
The self-paired middle row/column behaviour for odd-sized grids, and the `ndim != 2` fallback, are unreachable because the constructor always emits 6x6 grids.

Demonstrations are ignored. This is acceptable because the 2/5/8 colour roles are fixed task constants, not arbitrary per-episode lookups. The episode evidence checks do not cover this task, which is consistent with that.
The archived rule text contains self-corrections about earlier inspections. They do not affect the final rule, which agrees with the constructor.
required_context_checks: Confirm the host's D4 index convention is the standard one: 0-3 are rotations by k quarter-turns and 4-7 are the flipped variants. The odd-k axis selection is valid for any composition order, provided k counts quarter-turns.
